name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
title: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
answer: Citation auditing and good law checking is the practice of verifying that every authority cited in a brief or memo still says what it is claimed to say and has not been overruled, superseded, or quietly narrowed. It covers the full chain of authority: statutes, regulations, cases, and secondary sources, plus the internal consistency of the citations themselves. In an AI-assisted workflow the same discipline applies to machine-generated drafts, where a plausible-looking citation may point to a case that does not exist or to a holding that was later reversed. The work sits inside legal research and case strategy rather than standing alone, because a citation problem is usually a strategy problem waiting to surface.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Citation auditing and good law checking is the practice of verifying that every authority cited in a brief or memo still says what it is claimed to say and has not been overruled, superseded, or quietly narrowed. It covers the full chain of authority: statutes, regulations, cases, and secondary sources, plus the internal consistency of the citations themselves. In an AI-assisted workflow the same discipline applies to machine-generated drafts, where a plausible-looking citation may point to a case that does not exist or to a holding that was later reversed. The work sits inside legal research and case strategy rather than standing alone, because a citation problem is usually a strategy problem waiting to surface.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a citator, a primary law database, and the court record itself, with the citator flagging negative treatment and the database supplying the full text behind each flag. Firms typically pair a commercial citator with a docket service so that a pending appeal or a later order can be caught before filing. Where AI tools are used to assemble citations, a separate verification pass against the primary source is the control that keeps the tool honest. The output is a checked citation list, a short note on any authority that has moved, and a record of what was checked and when.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method is sequential and skeptical. Each citation is pulled from the draft, matched to its reporter or code cite, and read in the source rather than in the citing document. The citator is then run for negative treatment, and any signal is traced to the later opinion to see whether the earlier holding survived, was distinguished, or was replaced. Quotations and parentheticals are compared word by word against the original, and pin cites are confirmed against the page or paragraph. The final step is a second reader, because the person who wrote the citation is the least likely to notice that it no longer holds.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Responsibility for the audit sits with the filing lawyer, and the record of who checked what and when is the evidence that the duty was met. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing authority that was overruled or that never existed, and the rise of generative drafting has made that exposure more common. The site tracks 29 AI case law precedents and 152 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which is a reminder that the underlying law in this area is still moving and that a citation can age quickly. Confidentiality rules also apply, so client material should not be pasted into a public tool to check a cite. Nothing here is legal advice, and a firm's own supervision and conflicts procedures govern how the audit is documented.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward continuous checking rather than a single pass before filing. Courts are beginning to require disclosure when generative tools were used in drafting, and some judges have issued standing orders on the subject, which pushes verification earlier into the drafting process. Citator vendors are adding machine-readable treatment signals, and the harder problem is not finding negative treatment but judging whether a later case actually undermines the proposition being supported. Expect the audit trail itself, not just the corrected brief, to become the artifact that firms keep.
